title: 📌Kaipara harbour coastal
description:
***Join us on Sunday, October 4th for the Kaipara Coast to Shelly Beach Hike as we explore the shores of the Kaipara Harbour—the largest natural harbour in the Southern Hemisphere! Starting at South Head, we will make our way south along the coastline to Shelly Beach, taking in vast tidal flats, coastal farmland, sand beaches, and mangroves along the way. While no swimming is required, you can expect wading and some muddy patches, so come prepared to get partially wet. Please note that this hike requires a car shuttle, and details are in this description.***
📌 New members are welcome
📌 If you find yourself on the "waiting list" and decide to attend the hike on the day of the event, then please be aware that you will need to hike separately from the group. Only those listed as "Going" are considered valid participants.
There are no "plus ones"- If you want to go, then you will need to register with meetup
📌 Individuals who are unfit or prefer a slower pace are kindly requested not to RSVP. Slow people will hold up the group, as everyone will have to wait for you to catch up. There are alternative Meetup groups available for those who enjoy walking very slowly.
📌If you are unable to attend, please update your status to avoid a "No Show" being recorded next to your name. Accumulating three or more "No Shows" will result in your status being changed to "Not going." It is always polite to adjust your RSVP status if you can no longer participate. Thank you👍

title: Everyone's a Studio: Media, Culture and the Generation Era
description:
For a century, media meant pointing a camera or a microphone at something, and the cost of doing that decided what got made. That constraint is disappearing. Video, music, voices, 3D worlds and playable scenes can now be generated on demand, and captured reality itself is going volumetric: you can walk around inside a recorded moment.

This is a demo & discussion session: which trends are real, which are tech demos going nowhere, and what any of it does to society and culture. Bring your ideas and opinions.

We'll explore-

* The state of generation – video, image, music and voice: what's production-ready and what's still a party trick.
* From flat to volumetric – 3D, gaussian splats and 4DGS, explained plainly, and why they matter beyond the wow factor.
* Games and generated worlds – when environments, characters and story are made on the fly, what's left of a game as an authored thing?
* Entertainment for an audience of one – personalised media versus shared culture. What happens when nobody watched the same thing last night?
* Education – the infinitely patient tutor and the explainer built for exactly you, and whether anyone actually learns more.
* Who makes things now – production cost collapses. What that does to creative work, and who still gets paid.
* Trust and evidence – when any footage can be made, what counts as proof? Provenance, deepfakes, and the liar's dividend.
* The slop problem – infinite supply, finite attention. Do taste and curation become the scarce thing?

No prior background assumed. If you watch, play, make or teach, you have a stake in this.

Afterwards we usually continue over dinner nearby — a good chance to connect with fellow builders and practitioners.

title: Improverished Intermediate Workshop
description:
Nau mai haere mai to the brand new Improverished Intermediate Monthly Workshop! This is a brand new thing we are trying out and we're super excited about it!

Once a month, after our 2 hour open workshop we will be offering an extra 1 hour workshop specifically for people who've done a bit of improv and are looking for a bit of extension.

What to expect:
\- more scenework
\- more feedback and guidance from tutors
\- a chance to grow your improv skills
\- the usual friendly\, relaxed Improverished vibes

Who can attend:
\- we recommend this for folks who have been coming to our open workshops for at least a year \(even if you haven't made it every month\, that's fine\)
\- anyone who has improv experience outside of Improverished for at least 1 course
\- this class is for adults 18\+

This is not a structured 'Improv 201' type course, it's designed to be a regular drop-in option for those with some experience looking to do more improv with a bit more focus but still in a relaxed and casual environment.

Want to try improv for the first time? Try our monthly open workshop instead!

**Please note:** you are welcome to attend the workshop after attending our open workshop or as a stand-alone.

***RSVP's are necessary for numbers, we recommend a koha of $5-10 for the intermediate class***

*About us: Improverished is a joyful improvised theatre company established in 2015. We are passionate about welcoming, inclusive creative spaces as well as community connection and sharing the fun of improv!*

All workshops take place in Basement Theatre Maker's Space. This is located right next to Basement Theatre in the Grey's Ave carpark. If you haven't been before, hang out outside Basement Theatre and we'll find you there!

title: When I Saw You (Jordan 2012) 1.30 mins
description:
We are in a season of films on Sunday afternoon about films about life in a war zone, especially Palestine.
I have chosen films that are not propaganda.
The attempt is to lift ourselves above that and do a deep dive into the realities of life in such areas. In this film, Tarek and his mother, Ghaydaa, cross the border from Palestine to Jordan along with tens of thousands of other people.

**When I Saw You** was selected at as the Palestinian entry for the best foreign language film at the Academy Awards. The New York Times reviewer wrote:
"A soft-centered child's-eye view of alienation, toughened by fine acting and Hlne Louvart's full-bodied photography."

The Total Film reviewer wrote: "political without point-scoring, Jacir remains true to a child's-eye view, with Asfa's delightful, exuberant performance always upfront."

"Palestinian filmmaker Annemarie Jacir's second film is slight yet significant - and, because of the situation in Syria, timely - story about a boy whose courage inspires hope among the hopeless."

A must-see for us all as we a look into the lives of familes fleeing from war - anywhere.
